title: Let gratitude notice what mercy already did
summary: The shabad begins by admitting that the Lord's gifts went unrecognized. Gratitude becomes honest when it names the mercy it has been living on all along.
takeaway: Name the mercy you have been living on before complaint takes the room.
lifeApplication: Before asking for more, write one unnoticed gift in a full sentence and turn it into a brief ardaas of thanks.

source.shortMeaning: The line confesses that the Lord's work was present before the heart knew how to appreciate it.
source.lifeApplication: Name one gift you treated as ordinary, and let that confession become thanks rather than guilt.

evidence.coreClaim: Gratitude begins when unnoticed mercy is finally recognized as the Lord's doing.
evidence.turn: Let the confession be plain: I was already being helped before I knew how to thank the Helper.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before asking for more, write one unnoticed gift in a full sentence and turn it into a brief ardaas of thanks.
